messages.content:
Our list endpoints are starting to page through tables that change while people read
them, and page numbers repeat or skip rows when that happens. Please add cursor-based
pages to the pager package, next to the page-number helpers, and export everything
from src/index.ts:

- `paginateCursor(items, { limit, cursor })` returns `{ items, nextCursor, hasMore }`.
  The rows have a numeric `id`. The page holds the rows with the lowest ids after the
  cursor, in ascending id order (the first rows when there is no cursor), whatever the
  order of the input. `nextCursor` is null on the last page, and `hasMore` says whether
  there is a next page.
- A cursor is an opaque URL-safe string that stands for the last id the caller saw, not
  a position, so rows added or removed between two requests do not make the next page
  repeat or skip rows. Text that is not a cursor from `paginateCursor` is rejected with
  an `InvalidCursorError`, which should be exported too.
- `limit` follows the same page size rules as page-number pagination: 20 by default, 100
  at most (larger values are cut down to 100), and a value that is not a whole number of
  at least 1 is a `RangeError`. Add `parseCursorParams(query)`, which reads `cursor` and
  `limit` strings from a query the way `parsePageParams` reads `page` and `per_page`:
  no cursor gives `null`, and a bad `limit` is a `PageParamsError`.
- A query with both `page` and `cursor` is ambiguous, so `parsePageParams` should reject
  it with a `PageParamsError`. The tests the repository started with should keep passing.

The page-number helpers (`paginate`, `parsePageParams`, `pageLinks`, `linkHeader`) should
keep working as they do now.
